dimension_justifications.soundness: The internal arithmetic is verifiable and I checked it: from the fits printed in Table 5's footnote (p.21) and the retained means of Table 4 (p.20) I reproduced all four Table 1 rows (1978.6/1726.4=1.15x, 3493.3/1441.9=2.42x, 13893.2/1885.5=7.37x, 15057.2/2653.9=5.67x), all four crossovers (5.13/4.69/3.79/2.01) and the N=12.5 line crossing to the printed digit; 106.235/9.661=10.9963, 136.235/9.661=14.101, 136.235-106.235=30.000, 56.438/9.661=5.8419=3.9174x1.4912, and Table 22a's 88.68/92.87/93.06/94.01% all reconcile. The claim discipline is unusually honest: adverse transient, adverse TTFT against four references, an allocator component that 'saves nothing' against the right baseline, a self-refuted prediction, printed dispersion instead of averaged point estimates. Two substantive gaps remain. First, Table 1 -- the sole body table and the vehicle of the headline regime claim -- pairs S measured on the private-materialization deployment path with T measured on the shared-entry composition path, and never says so; Table 5 also prints the private fit (790.50+148.38N), under which the N=8 crossover moves from 2.01 to ~4.3 documents and the D=4,N=8 row flips sign (2016.2 vs 1978.6 MiB). The caption enumerates three unmeasured assumptions and omits this choice. Second, the paper's one interval that excludes zero has upper endpoint -0.0390, smaller than the +/-0.20 F1 resample noise Appendix B itself documents between Table 2 and Table 4; the text concedes 'a different resample sequence could carry it across' yet still reports the ordering as 'supported'. Add the disclosed facts that the primary audit never ran on the deployed code path, that timing resolves nothing at three repeats, that a dense-TPOT discrepancy is flagged and not reconciled, and that every headline ratio in the abstract (7.37x, 5.67x, 'two at N=8') is a model output from a workload shape never executed, and the plausible core carries gaps that materially reduce confidence.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The section skeleton is genuinely coherent -- read alone, the topic sentences of Sections 1, 2, 3, 4.1-4.4, 5.1-5.7 and 6 form one line: capacity budget (Eq. 1), what a hybrid entry must retain (Eq. 2), how it is packed (Eq. 3), how it is forked and audited, the cohorts, term S, term T, their sum, the limits. Motivation does set up Methodology and Methodology does set up Experiments. Execution defeats the skeleton. The body carries one figure and one table, and that table contains no measurement -- it is arithmetic over two appendix tables. Every measured quantity behind Sections 5.2-5.6 lives in an appendix: retained state and F1 in Table 4 (p.20), transient in Table 5 (p.21), latency in Table 22 (p.35), allocator endpoints in Table 19 (p.33), audit verdicts in Tables 9-10 (p.26). A referee cannot check one number of the central claim from pages 1-9. The abstract runs ~570 words across pages 1-2 and reads as a compressed limitations section. Figure 3 (p.22) is never cross-referenced from any text; Figure 2 (p.18), the only figure explaining split geometry and bit policy, is cited once parenthetically for a side point. An unnumbered, uncaptioned matrix heads p.28, introduced a full page earlier and un-referenceable. Table 22 is printed before Table 21 on p.35. At least six tables carry a fully constant column (Tables 9, 10, 11, 12, 30 and the p.28 matrix), Tables 9 and 10 largely duplicate each other, and Table 4's TTFT column is empty for its entire archival block. Section 4.2 and Figure 2's caption both state 'we do not call it Q16', yet Table 23 (p.36) uses Q16 as a cell value and three times in its footnote. Arm names drift between tables reporting identical numbers. Body prose averages 43 words per sentence (median 38, max 165; 33% over 50 words; 11.5 semicolons and 6.2 em-dashes per 1000 words; 45% of sentences carrying an explicit negation). Main text spills two Conclusion lines onto p.10. This is squarely 'understandable, but organization, figures, and writing materially obstruct evaluation'.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The honest framing -- report total memory M_total(D,N) = S*D + T(N) rather than the retained term alone, and let the second term run against you -- is a useful corrective for a literature that quotes compression ratios, and the whole-entry hybrid denominator (residual plus lower attention KV plus convolution/recurrent state) is a real accounting improvement over CoMem's residual-only figure. The negative results are of community value. But the paper disclaims its own mechanisms in Section 2 (group-wise asymmetric quantization, per-layer mixed precision, split replay, quantize-and-recompute all attributed to prior art, XQuant named as closest); the sharing demonstration moves 0.500 of 12.938 MiB, about 4% of per-request state, and the paper says so; the ownership component 'saves nothing' against the paper's own paged-prefix baseline; there is no latency, throughput, admitted-capacity or recall result; and everything sits on one model, one GPU family, 60 items, no replication. What remains is a careful single-stack measurement study of a known composition -- narrow and of uncertain significance beyond the specific stack.

paper_summary: Q-CoMem extends CoMem's split-replay interface to a hybrid (attention + gated-delta-network) LLM. An offline Write runs a document through layers [0,j), then group-quantizes the depth-j boundary residual together with the lower-layer full-attention KV and convolution/recurrent state under per-layer, per-state-type bit widths (Eq. 2-3). An online Read dequantizes the entry, exposes immutable document tensors, creates request-local mutable state via copy-on-write and recurrent rebinding, replays the query through the lower layers and reconstructs the suffix. A companion component, ForkAudit, validates the ownership discipline with seven contract targets (plus three packed-entry obligations) under fail-closed coverage/verdict separation. Evaluation runs Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on H20-3e across four separate executions: a 60-item archival Qasper/2WikiMQA Store-F1 panel, a 60-item operating-point run with timing, a 96-configuration vLLM ownership factorial on PG-19, and an eight-item composition run that shares one packed depth-7 entry across N in {1,2,4,8}. Headline results: a frozen Q4/Q4/Q8 depth-7 policy cuts retained state per document from 106.235 to 9.661 MiB against an all-BF16 reference (10.9965x; 14.10x against the stack's native-dtype 136.235 MiB) at -0.45 [-2.06, 0.99] mean F1; peak transient allocation runs the other way, exceeding the exact cache at every measured fanout; their sum names a regime rather than a ratio, with Q-CoMem smaller above roughly five warm documents at N=1 and two at N=8. Timing is adverse against exact reuse, dense recomputation, SGLang Radix and a published HYPIC prefix cache. The paper explicitly claims no latency, capacity, recall, edge or broad-quality result.
strongest_verified_contribution: The two-term memory model and its adverse second term. The paper measures both quantities a caching method actually controls -- retained bytes per warm document and peak transient allocation per concurrent query -- and reports their sum rather than the compression ratio alone. I verified the model end to end from printed inputs: Table 5's fits (full-prefix 103.45+166.28N, shared 809.68+109.76N) and Table 4's means (136.235 and 9.661 MiB/document) reproduce every Table 1 cell, every crossover, and the N=12.5 line crossing exactly. The finding that a method which cuts retained state 11-14x simultaneously allocates 3.25x more transient memory at N=1 and still more at every measured fanout, so that the advantage exists only above a warm-set threshold, is a genuinely useful and self-refuting result that most papers in this area would not have measured or printed.
strengths: The section skeleton carries one argument. Read in isolation, the topic sentences of Sections 1 through 6 form a single line of reasoning -- capacity budget, what a hybrid entry must retain, how it is packed, how it is forked, how ownership is audited, the two terms, their sum, the limits -- and Motivation (Eq. 1, p.4) genuinely sets up Methodology (Eq. 2, p.4), which genuinely sets up the experiment sections.

Exemplary claim discipline. Section 5.3 opens 'is not a speedup'; Section 5.5's second paragraph concedes 'the ownership component saves nothing' against the right baseline; Section 5.6's second paragraph is headed 'Transient allocation refutes an arithmetic prediction of ours'; Section 5.2 decomposes its own 5.84x into 3.9174x split and 1.4912x width and says only the former is a split-replay advantage. Confident language is conspicuously absent where evidence is thin.

Dispersion is printed rather than averaged away. Table 22(b) (p.35) gives min/median/max per timing cell, exposing a 404.01 ms TPOT maximum against a 53.45 ms median and a median of four generated tokens against a 32-token cap, and Section 5.3 then reads the paper's own timing evidence as weaker.

Every number I checked reconciles. All four Table 1 rows, all four crossovers, the N=12.5 crossing, 10.9965x, 14.10x, the 30.000 MiB FP32 excess, 5.8419 = 3.9174 x 1.4912, and Table 22a's four reduction percentages against 140.34 MiB all reproduce from printed inputs.

Figure 1 (p.3) is a clear, correctly captioned protocol schematic that states its own scope limit -- that the ForkAudit rail is not an execution stage and that the packed Read path drawn is not the path behind Tables 4 and 22.

Captions and footnotes are conscientious. Table 1's footnote enumerates three unmeasured assumptions and states that no workload of the shape its rows describe was executed; Table 20's caption forbids reading it as a leaderboard; Table 8 authorizes each cohort to a specific claim and lists explicit exclusions.

Ethics, LLM-use and reproducibility statements are present, placed before the references (p.10), and the reproducibility statement names precisely which components are not archived and states that Table 4 is replayable but not re-executable.
questions: Table 1's caption says T(N) comes from 'the measured transient fits of Table 5', but Table 5 prints three fits. Section 5.6 uses the shared-entry fit 809.68+109.76N. Why is it legitimate to pair that with S measured on the private-materialization path that Section 5.7 says is 'not identical in implementation'? Please print Table 1 a second time under the private fit 790.50+148.38N, since that is the arm behind Tables 4 and 22, and state which of the two a deployment should budget from.

The composition run's ten-target coverage and verdicts are asserted in one prose sentence (Section 5.6, p.8) and one authorization row (Table 8, p.25), but no table anywhere reports them. Will you print a per-target coverage/verdict table for the packed path, with the same columns as Table 10, and state the pass predicates of the three packed-entry obligations (dequantized-view immutability, residual-chunk binding, packed-entry lifetime)?

Appendix B documents up to 0.20 F1 points of resample-sequence movement between Table 2 and Table 4 for the same comparison. The headline pairwise interval's upper endpoint is -0.0390. Under a 0.20-point noise floor, on what basis is 'the ordering is supported on this cohort' a stronger statement than 'observed'? Would averaging over the five seeds you already ran move that endpoint across zero?

Can Table 4 and Table 5 move into Sections 5.2 and 5.6? Pages 19, 21, 30, 31 and 33 each carry 30-50% white space, and demoting Tables 9-12 -- which share two constant columns and duplicate each other's target list -- would free the equivalent body space.

Section 4.2 and Figure 2's caption both state 'we do not call it Q16', yet Table 23 (p.36) uses Q16 as a cell value and three times in its footnote for exactly that arm. Which is the term of record? Relatedly, should 'Q-CoMem split Q8' (Table 22a) and 'Q-CoMem state / Q8' (Table 23) be one name, and likewise 'calibrated per-layer' and 'per-layer mixed' (both 9.74 MiB)?
Figure 3 (p.22) is not cited from any text. Is it intended to be referenced from Section 5.5 or from Appendix D's opening?
The Conclusion's last two lines fall on page 10. Was the 9-page ICLR limit checked against the compiled PDF rather than the source?

issues.observed_evidence: The abstract runs approximately 570 words and spans two pages, occupying all of page 1 below the title and the top eleven lines of page 2. Body prose measured over pages 1-9 averages 43.1 words per sentence (median 38, maximum 165), with 32.9% of sentences over 50 words, 11.5 semicolons and 6.2 em-dashes per 1000 words, and 45.5% of sentences carrying an explicit negation or caveat.
issues.why_it_matters: The abstract does deliver what the body delivers -- I found no over-promise -- but it delivers it in the wrong register: it functions as a compressed limitations section rather than as an abstract, and a reader cannot extract the claim from it in one pass. Combined with 43-word mean sentences throughout the body, this is the mechanism by which an argument with a sound skeleton becomes hard to evaluate. Reviewers and readers triage on the abstract; a two-page one that leads with caveats will be misread as either evasive or unsummarizable, neither of which the underlying work deserves.
issues.required_fix: Cut the abstract to 200-250 words on one page. issues.location: Table 2 pp.17-18 (continuation header at top of p.18); Table 2 caption p.17; Appendix B p.16 lines 850-853
issues.observed_evidence: Table 2 spans pages 17-18. Its page-17 header is 'Configuration | Subset | Delta-F1 | 95% CI' and its first two blocks have four columns matching it. Its third block, 'Archival analysis; reference arm as listed (24 intervals)', has different columns -- Configuration, Reference arm, Subset, 95% CI -- with no Delta-F1 point estimate at all. On page 18 the continuation prints BOTH headers stacked: the original four-column header and then a second 'Configuration | Reference arm | Subset | 95% CI' row. Separately, the same comparison is printed with different numbers in two tables: Table 4's j=7 row reads -0.37 [-1.97, 1.08] while Table 2's corresponding row reads +0.3708 [-1.0533, +2.0345] (i.e. [-2.03, 1.05]); the full-prefix-Q8 row reads [-9.12, 0.32] in Table 4 and negates to [-9.32, 0.19] from Table 2. Appendix B discloses the cause ('their endpoints agree with the printed ones to within 0.20 F1 points -- the resampling noise of an independently drawn resample sequence') in running prose on p.16.
issues.why_it_matters: The stacked, mutually inconsistent continuation header makes the third block of a 52-row table unreadable at first encounter, and the caption's promise of '52 paired-bootstrap intervals' is delivered with no point estimate for 24 of them under a header that names a Delta-F1 column. Separately, a reader who cross-checks Table 4 against Table 2 -- exactly what the complete-inventory appendix invites -- meets a numerical mismatch before meeting its explanation, and the explanation is buried mid-paragraph. The disclosure is honest, but it should be adjacent to the numbers. The 0.20-point noise floor also bears directly on the headline interval whose upper endpoint is -0.0390 (issue 09).
issues.required_fix: Split Table 2's third block into its own numbered table with its own header, or add the Delta-F1 column to it. Fix the longtable continuation so exactly one header repeats. Add a footnote to both Table 2 and Table 4 stating that endpoints from independently drawn resample sequences differ by up to 0.20 F1 points and pointing to Appendix B.
issues.verification_test: Confirm the page-18 continuation shows one header consistent with the rows beneath it; confirm every interval in Table 2 carries a point estimate; confirm the noise-floor footnote appears on both tables.

issues.location: Section 5.4 p.7 lines 350-358; Abstract p.1 lines 046-049; Appendix B p.16 lines 850-857
issues.observed_evidence: The paper's one interval that excludes zero is full-prefix Q8 minus frozen j=7 = -3.4122 [-8.4296, -0.0390], and Section 5.4 concludes 'excluding zero, so the ordering is supported on this cohort rather than merely observed.' Appendix B (p.16) documents that endpoints from an independently drawn resample sequence move by up to 0.20 F1 points, and that across five seeds the frozen row's endpoints move by up to 0.075. The upper endpoint -0.0390 is smaller in magnitude than both figures. Section 5.4 itself concedes 'a different resample sequence could carry it across', and the abstract concedes 'excluding zero by 0.0390 -- enough for the ordering, not to call the effect large or robust'.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper is nearly right about this and then takes one step too far. If the documented Monte-Carlo movement exceeds the margin by which the interval excludes zero, the correct statement is that the sign is not resolved by this analysis, not that 'the ordering is supported ... rather than merely observed'. The distinction matters because this is the only inferential separation the paper claims anywhere, and it is one of the two results the abstract advances against a competing method.
issues.required_fix: Either increase the resample count and/or average over seeds until the interval's exclusion of zero exceeds the documented noise floor, and report the seed-averaged endpoints; or downgrade the language in Section 5.4 and the abstract to 'the sign is not resolved at this resample precision' and drop 'supported ... rather than merely observed'.
issues.verification_test: Recompute the interval at 100,000 resamples across the five recorded seeds and report the range of upper endpoints. If any seed yields an upper endpoint above zero, the ordering claim must be withdrawn.
issues.evidence_needed: Re-analysis of the archived per-item F1 values the reproducibility statement says are retained; no new GPU execution.

ethics_concerns: No ethics concerns. The Ethics Statement (p.10) is present and appropriate: no human-subject data, public PG-19 and LongBench-v1 (Qasper/2WikiMQA) corpora, an explicit statement that model safety, bias and privacy are not assessed, and an acknowledgement that efficiency gains may increase the scale of model use. review_limitations: PDF-only access. I could not inspect the LaTeX source, the repository, the anonymous supplement, or any evidence file, so every provenance statement in Appendix A and Appendix J is taken on the manuscript's word and none of the archived artifacts, hashes or replay counts was verified.

I verified the arithmetic of Table 1, the ratios of Sections 5.2-5.4, the Table 22a reduction percentages and the Table 5 least-squares fits by recomputation from printed values, but I did not attempt to re-derive Table 3's per-component byte counts, Appendix B's 52 intervals, or any ForkAudit count.

My inference in issue 01 that Table 1 uses Table 5's shared-entry fit rests on reproducing all four cells and all four crossovers to the printed digit and on Section 5.6's explicit naming of 809.68 + 109.76N; if the authors intend S to be arm-independent (which is defensible for a stored-entry byte count) the soundness component of that issue softens to a disclosure failure, but the clarity component stands.

Font sizes were estimated from word bounding-box heights calibrated against 10pt body text rather than read from the font dictionaries, so the ~7pt (scriptsize) figure for table footnotes is approximate.

I am not in a position to judge whether the hybrid split-replay entry is novel relative to unpublished or concurrent work; my contribution score reflects the positioning the paper itself argues in Section 2 and Appendix G, where most mechanisms are explicitly disclaimed as prior art.
My role is clarity and presentation; the soundness score reflects what I could check from the PDF and should be weighted against reviewers with repository access.
